subtitulo: Keeping going when the word won't come
descripcion: Most courses teach you to build sentences. Almost none teach you what to do when you are halfway through one and the word won't come. That gap is why people who know a lot of English still go quiet in conversation. The moves are few and they are learnable by heart.

filas: get in without waiting for silence
*Can I say something?* / *Sorry, can I just add —*
*Hold on, let me think.* / *What's the word… give me a second.*
*Sorry, let me say that again.* / *That's not what I meant.*
cuadroReferencia.notaPie: *Filled pauses — *well*, *so*, *I mean*, *right* — keep the turn. Silence gives it away.*

ejemplos.texto: *Hold on, let me think how to say this.*
*Sorry, let me say that again — I meant the opposite.*
*What's the word… give me a second.*

notas: Saying out loud that you are looking for a word is normal. Native speakers do it constantly.
Never apologise for your English mid-conversation. It moves the other person's attention onto your level instead of your point. Say *give me a second* instead.
Asking someone to repeat is a skill, not a failure: *Sorry, could you say that again?*

es.en: Spanish takes the floor with short signals («perdona», «oye»), while English usually announces the turn (Sorry, can I just say something?). Adding such a phrase makes the turn sound polite rather than abrupt.
es.es: El español toma la palabra con señales breves («perdona», «oye»), mientras que el inglés suele anunciar el turno («Sorry, can I just say something?»). Añadir esa frase hace que la intervención suene cortés y no brusca.

de.en: «Darf ich kurz was sagen?» corresponds exactly to Can I just say something?, with «kurz» doing the work of just. Taking the floor therefore transfers directly.
de.de: «Darf ich kurz was sagen?» entspricht genau «Can I just say something?», wobei «kurz» die Funktion von «just» übernimmt. Das Ergreifen des Wortes lässt sich daher direkt übertragen.

it.en: «Posso dire una cosa?» corresponds to Can I say something?; English adds just to soften it (Can I just say something?).
it.it: «Posso dire una cosa?» corrisponde a «Can I say something?»; l'inglese aggiunge «just» per attenuare («Can I just say something?»).

fr.en: «Je peux dire quelque chose ?» corresponds to Can I say something?; English adds just to soften it (Can I just say something?).
fr.fr: «Je peux dire quelque chose ?» correspond à «Can I say something?» ; l'anglais ajoute souvent «just» pour adoucir : «Can I just say something?».

pt.en: «Posso só dizer uma coisa?» corresponds exactly to Can I just say something?, with «só» doing the work of just.
pt.pt: «Posso só dizer uma coisa?» corresponde exatamente a «Can I just say something?», com «só» fazendo o papel de «just».

errores: *Sorry, my English is bad.* Never say this.
Going silent while thinking, which hands the turn to the other person.
Abandoning a sentence halfway instead of repairing it out loud.
Waiting for a clear gap that never comes.

es: «*Este…*» as a thinking filler rendered as *This…* instead of *Um…* or *Let me see…*.
de: «*Also*» as a filler rendered as *Also…* instead of *So…* or *Well…*.
it: «*Cioè*» carried over as *That is* in every sentence instead of *I mean*.
fr: «*Bon*» as a filler rendered as *Good…* instead of *Right…* or *Well…*.
pt: «*Pronto*» as a filler rendered as *Ready…* instead of *Right…* or *OK, so…*.

traducciones.de: Entschuldige, darf ich nur kurz ergänzen —
Wie heißt das Wort noch mal…

traducciones.fr: Ce n’est pas ce que je voulais dire.
traducciones.pt: Não foi isso que eu quis dizer.

redemittel.expresion: Sorry, could you say that again?

mision.consigna: Explain to someone what you do to stay fit, without stopping when you lose a word.
requisitos: two fillers that keep your turn (*Hold on, let me think*)
one self-correction (*Let me say that again*)
one question handing over the turn
use *to stay fit*, *to reduce stress* and *wellbeing*

microtareas.texto: Write three phrases you'll use when you forget a word.
Talk about your *diet* for one minute without stopping. When you stall, use a phrase.
Record 90 seconds on *wellbeing*. End with *What do you think?*

autochequeo: Did I take the turn with words, or wait for a gap?
Did I stay silent while thinking?
Did I repair out loud, or give up on the sentence?
Did I apologise for my English?
Did I hand the turn back at least twice?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on how I manage the conversation. (1) Mark every move: taking, holding, repairing, giving the turn. (2) Flag where I gave up on a sentence instead of repairing it. (3) Flag any apology for my English. (4) Give me three more phrases for buying time. Do not correct anything else.
